overview: Maya history encompasses distinct societies and city-states. Tikal, Calakmul, Palenque and Copan supported royal courts with specialized artists; their political histories should be explored individually rather than compressed into one Maya empire.

items.text: Some court artists signed their work. The sculptor Chakalte' left his name on a relief showing Shield Jaguar IV receiving tribute.
Stoneworkers carved and polished limestone vessels with tools and abrasives. Shell, bone, jade and fired clay offered other media for intricate objects.
Blue-green jade evoked water, new growth and primordial beings. It became material for offerings, ornaments and royal regalia.
Tikal's carved and painted inscriptions preserve dynastic history and relationships with other cities. They document particular courts, not a single pan-Maya government.
Tikal combined monumental precincts with residential districts and reservoirs known today as aguadas. Its surrounding settlements also supported agricultural production.
After several Classic-period kingdoms declined, northern centers such as Chichen Itza continued commissioning major artworks. Political collapse in one region did not end Maya history everywhere.
